correctness.rationale: In the invariant sector y=-x in (0,1), p in (0,1), the SIS equation is pdot=-beta p[y+(1-y)p], hence p<=p0/(1+beta p0t). For kx<1/3, F(y,0)=tanh(y+kx y³)-y<0 from arctanh y>y+y³/3. Comparison with z-dot=F(z,0)/tau yields y>=z~(At)^-1/2, so p<=C e^{-a sqrt t} and py^-2=O(t e^{-a sqrt t}). With w=y^-2 and c=1/3-kx,d=2/15-kx, exact Taylor gives wdot=A-2d/(tau w)-2kp p w/tau+O(p+w^-2). Integrable errors yield w=At-(d/c) log t+K+o(1). Thus y=(At)^-1/2+O(log t/t^(3/2)); the correction and (1-y)p are integrable, giving a finite positive limit for p exp(beta sqrt(2tau/c) sqrt t). Neutral x0=0 is invariant with p=p0/(1+beta p0t). Proof is global for every strict negative-opinion interior initial point under fixed stated parameters.
